clue.text: Primates sobbing after conversion

indicators.note: letters that have undergone a conversion have been changed into a new form, so the word sobbing is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone describes apes left weeping after some kind of conversion experience.
explanation.definitionFit: These long-armed apes of South-East Asia belong to the primate order.

clue.text: A stocking-filler turning to ice

indicators.note: turning signals that the phrase A stocking-filler is read the other way round

parts.note: a leg is what fills a stocking

explanation.surface: A Christmas stocking present apparently turns into ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stocking-filler' looks like a small Christmas present, but it is the limb inside the stocking; 'turning' reverses the whole phrase 'A stocking-filler'.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian ice cream is commonly called an ice, and gelato is that frozen dessert.

clue.text: See 20
Done with seat of power, say, ousted

parts.note: something done with is over, finished

indicators.note: say signals the word is spoken, giving a sound-alike spelt differently

parts.note: a throne is the seat of a monarch's power

explanation.surface: A ruler finished with the seat of power has been removed from office.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposed ruler has been toppled, which is the sense of the clue's removal from power.

clue.text: Difficult subject for a pathologist

definitions.meaning: a ... test or climb is a hard one
slang for a corpse, the body a pathologist examines

explanation.surface: A tough case faces a pathologist.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff means hard to do, and it is also slang for a dead body on the mortuary table.

clue.text: Time off, stuff punctuated by irregular pay

indicators.note: something punctuated by another thing has that thing breaking into it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: gear means stuff, belongings

indicators.note: irregular means out of order, so the word pay is rearranged

explanation.surface: Taking time off is a matter of possessions and patchy wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' looks like a verb here but is the noun, belongings.
explanation.definitionFit: A year taken out between school and university or work is a break from study.

clue.text: Marked by degrees — now possessing one?

definitions.meaning: a measuring jug or thermometer is marked with a scale of steps
a student who has finished university now holds a degree

explanation.surface: Something scaled in degrees also seems to hold a degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A scale divided into steps is calibrated, and a person awarded a degree has completed their course.

clue.text: Care taken with lad up for bullying, as newspaper editor

indicators.note: bullying knocks things about, so these letters are pushed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor is mocked as someone who took up a boy in order to bully him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken with' joins the two lots of fodder, CARE and LAD UP, which 'bullying' rearranges. He was editor of the Daily Mail, a British tabloid, for over twenty-five years.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-serving editor of the Daily Mail newspaper, known for his combative style.

clue.text: Removal van is coming to Istanbul, every capital in time

indicators.note: in signals that the initials are placed inside the word for time

parts.note: an eon is a vast stretch of time

indicators.note: every capital means take the capital, first, letter of each word

explanation.surface: A removal van heads for Istanbul, as if moving house to the Turkish capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Every capital' takes V, I, C, T, I from van is coming to Istanbul, set 'in' EON.
explanation.definitionFit: Forcing a tenant out of a property is the act of removing them from it.

clue.text: Losers of nuts describing unfinished construction?

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so these letters go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some people who have lost their nuts are being described.
explanation.definitionFit: A building still lacking its top covering is incomplete, so the adjective describes a half-built house.

clue.text: Smoother bubbles having wiped rear

indicators.note: having the rear wiped off means the last letter is removed

parts.note: lather is the froth of soap bubbles

explanation.surface: Something that smooths by bubbling has had its bottom wiped.
explanation.definitionFit: A turning machine shapes and smooths wood or metal as it spins, so it is a tool for smoothing.

clue.text: A flower was mine, nothing for old actress

parts.note: I'd is short for I had, so something was mine
a lupin is a tall garden flower
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone recalls owning a flower, then gave it up for nothing to a former star.
explanation.definitionFit: She was a Hollywood film star and director of the 1940s and 1950s, so a performer from long ago.

clue.text: A DH our say?

parts.note: a dingbat: the letters H OUR sit within A D, a picture of hours inside a day

explanation.surface: A scrap of garbled text, as if someone mumbled half a phrase about our day.
explanation.walkthrough: A picture clue: A D with H OUR inside it shows hours contained in a day, and 'say' marks the answer as just one way of putting how many.
explanation.definitionFit: A full day lasts this number of hours, as in a round-the-clock shop.

clue.text: And the others still expected to return

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: someone late has not arrived yet and is still expected

explanation.surface: The rest of the party is still awaited back home.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin abbreviation in a list of names means and other people.

clue.text: Inebriate movement beyond comprehension

definitions.meaning: the lurching walk of a drunk person
astonishing, too amazing to take in

explanation.surface: A drunk's walk is somehow incomprehensible.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the reeling gait of a drunk and also means astounding.

clue.text: Disproving statements, suspect is fortunate

indicators.note: suspect means dodgy, not to be trusted as written, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lucky is doubted when arguments are being rebutted.
explanation.definitionFit: Arguments that show a claim to be false are rebuttals of it.

clue.text: Loud chains of iron, not one little bit?

indicators.note: chains means holds fast, so one piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: forte is the musical direction for loud
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Heavy iron chains clank loudly, not a bit of them quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chains' looks like iron fetters but is the container signal. The phrase comes from saying someone can't sing for toffee.
explanation.definitionFit: In the idiom about being unable to do something, the phrase means not at all, not in the slightest.

clue.text: Chance to keep strike, as inconsistency afoot?

indicators.note: to keep is to hold, so the word for chance holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: odds express the chance of something happening
to sock is to punch, strike

explanation.surface: There's a chance of a strike, and so trouble is afoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Afoot' usually means under way; here it means literally on the feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Mismatched hosiery is a lack of matching on the feet.

clue.text: Cat grabbing end of bow, fiddles

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing hold, so the cat's name holds the letter inside it

parts.note: Tiddles is a stock British name for a pet cat

indicators.note: end of means take the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cat snatches at the bow while someone plays the fiddle.
explanation.walkthrough: TIDDLES is the stereotypical name for a British house cat; the end of 'bow' is W.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidgeting with something idly is playing about with it, fiddling.

clue.text: Stretcher required, as setter in decline?

definitions.meaning: a yoga pose, something you stretch in
a setter is a dog breed, and in decline means heading down

explanation.surface: A stretcher is needed because the setter is falling ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' wants to be the crossword compiler; it is the gun dog. 'Stretcher' is not for carrying the sick but a stretching pose.
explanation.definitionFit: This yoga position stretches the back and legs, and read literally it is a hound pointing downhill.

clue.text: Pin more distorted?

definitions.meaning: a long pin used to hold meat together for cooking
read as skew plus -er, more askew

explanation.surface: A pin that is even more bent out of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A kebab spike pins meat, and as a mock comparative of skew it means more twisted.

clue.text: Seasonal fare connecting Blitzen's head with rutting stag?

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word

parts.note: a rutting animal is in heat, randy
a stag butts with its antlers, so it is one that butts

explanation.surface: Christmas food that links Santa's reindeer with a stag in the mating season.
explanation.walkthrough: Blitzen is one of Santa's reindeer. The sweet brandy-flavoured butter is a British accompaniment to Christmas pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: This rich spirit-flavoured sauce is eaten at Christmas, so it is festive food.

clue.text: Face Arsenal, for example?

definitions.meaning: one face of a cube is a surface
Arsenal is a London football club, a team

explanation.surface: An instruction to take on a football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face' reads as a verb, to play against; it is the noun, a surface. Arsenal is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface of an object is one of its faces, and a sports team is called this.

clue.text: Rolling Stones member, one kissing the drummer?

parts.note: Ronnie Wood is a guitarist in the Rolling Stones
one who gives a peck, a quick kiss

explanation.surface: A Rolling Stone is said to be kissing the band's drummer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The drummer' looks like the band's percussionist; it is the bird that drums on trees.
explanation.definitionFit: This bird hammers rapidly on tree trunks, so it is a natural drummer.

clue.text: See 6
So the hideous thing's erect

indicators.note: erect means standing upright, so in a down clue the word reads from the bottom up

parts.note: an ogre is a hideous monster

explanation.surface: The monster is standing upright, so it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word meaning therefore is used to introduce a conclusion.

clue.text: Opening cut on source of veal, not entirely fatty

indicators.note: on signals one piece is placed after the other in the across answer
not entirely means a word is left short of its last letter

parts.note: veal is meat from a calf

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: an orifice is an opening

explanation.surface: A butcher's first cut on a calf exposes fatty meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' drops F from CALF and 'cut' drops E from ORIFICE, giving CAL and ORIFIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Food high in calories is loosely called this, so rich and fattening.

clue.text: Faint on moon, one in a state?

indicators.note: on signals that one piece follows the other in the across answer

parts.note: Io is a moon of Jupiter
wan means pale, faint

explanation.surface: Someone feels faint over the moon, rather worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state' looks like being agitated; it means living in a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident of the US state of Iowa is a person living in a state.

clue.text: Pussycat's heart lifted, detecting some heartbeat

indicators.note: heart means the middle letters of the word

parts.note: lifted means stole, took

explanation.surface: A cat's heart is lifted when it detects a heartbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of PUSSYCAT is SY, its central two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The contraction phase of the heart is one part of each beat.

clue.text: With some enthusiasm, front and back to glue in antique

indicators.note: in signals these letters sit inside the word for antique

parts.note: early means from long ago, antique

indicators.note: front and back means the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Keenly gluing the front and back of an antique together.
explanation.walkthrough: The front and back of 'glue' are G and E, placed in EARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something keenly is doing it with enthusiasm.
